1366.1001.0.description:
Log TestSet setup outcome

Test-harness step (not a functional test): logs the per-test-set setup outcome before the set's functional cases run. Excluded from manual-test coverage mapping.

1366.1001.1.description:
Verify 3 different vlans can be configured with same ip address when configured under different VRF instances

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies that the same IP address can be configured on multiple VLANs simultaneously as long as each VLAN belongs to a different VRF-Lite instance. Assigns several VLANs to separate VRF instances, configures the overlapping IP on each, and confirms every VLAN holds the correct address and is associated with its expected VRF instance.

1366.1001.2.description:
Apply then remove VRF instances from vlans and verify same ip cannot be configured on different vlans after removal of VRF instances

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies that overlapping IP addresses are only permitted while the VLANs sit in distinct VRF instances. Configures VLANs under separate VRFs with the same IP, then removes the VRF associations and confirms the switch rejects the duplicate IP once the VLANs are back in the global/default table.

1366.1001.3.description:
Verify ip address configured on default and non-default vlan assigned to a VRF is reachable via ping

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies that an IP interface on a VLAN assigned to a non-default VRF is reachable, and that a default-VLAN address still works alongside it. Configures the addresses under the VRF and confirms reachability via ping.

1366.1001.4.description:
Verify dynamic ARP entries in VRF associated vlan is correctly created and can be cleared from CLI

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies dynamic ARP learning within a VRF-associated VLAN. Pings across the VRF interface to populate a dynamic ARP entry, confirms the entry appears in that VRF's ARP table, then clears the VRF ARP cache from the CLI and confirms the entry is removed.

1366.1001.5.description:
Verify dynamic ARP entries for same ip address can co-exist on 3 different VRF instances

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies that identical IP addresses can have co-existing dynamic ARP entries across multiple VRF instances. Configures the overlapping addresses under separate VRFs, generates dynamic ARP entries, and confirms each VRF's ARP table independently holds its own entry for the shared IP.

1366.1001.6.description:
Verify dynamic ARP entries for a VRF instance can be cleared without any impact on other VRF instances

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies VRF ARP-table isolation when clearing entries. Populates dynamic ARP entries in multiple VRF instances, clears the ARP cache for one instance, and confirms only that instance's entries are removed while the other VRFs' ARP entries remain intact.

1366.1001.7.description:
Verify static ARP entries for same ip address can co-exist on 3 different VRF instances

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies that identical static ARP entries can co-exist across multiple VRF instances. Configures the same IP-to-MAC static ARP binding under separate VRFs and confirms each VRF's ARP table independently shows its own static entry for the shared address.

1366.1003.1.description:
Test checks OSPF routing works between DUT and connected device and ospf learnt routes are correctly installed.

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies OSPF route learning in the global/default routing table. Establishes OSPF adjacency between the DUT and a connected device and confirms the remote network advertised via OSPF is correctly installed in the DUT's IP routing table.

1366.1003.2.description:
Test checks OSPF routing works between DUT and connected device and remote interface learnt via OSPF is reachable.

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies OSPF reachability in the global/default routing table. Establishes OSPF between the DUT and a connected device and confirms the remote interface learnt via OSPF is reachable (ping).

1366.1003.3.description:
Test checks OSPF routing works under a VRF instance and OSPF learnt routes are correctly installed.

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies OSPF route learning inside a VRF instance. Configures OSPF under a named VRF and confirms routes advertised via OSPF are correctly installed in that VRF's routing table.

1366.1003.4.description:
Test checks OSPF routing works under a VRF and remote interface learnt via OSPF is reachable with VRF.

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies OSPF reachability inside a VRF instance. Configures OSPF under a named VRF and confirms the remote interface learnt via OSPF is reachable within that VRF.

1366.1003.5.description:
Test checks BGP routing works between DUT and connected device and BGP learnt routes are correctly installed.

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies BGP route learning in the global/default routing table. Establishes a BGP session between the DUT and a connected device and confirms routes advertised via BGP are correctly installed in the DUT's IP routing table.

1366.1003.6.description:
Test checks BGP routing works between DUT and connected device and routes learnt via BGP is correctly installed.

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies BGP route installation in the global/default routing table. Establishes a BGP session between the DUT and a connected device and confirms the learnt routes are correctly installed.

1366.1003.7.description:
Test checks BGP routing works between DUT and connected device and BGP learnt routes are correctly installed when running under a vrf instance

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies BGP route learning inside a VRF instance. Configures BGP under a named VRF and confirms routes advertised via BGP are correctly installed in that VRF's routing table.

1366.1003.8.description:
Test checks BGP routing works between DUT and connected device and BGP learnt remote network is reachable when running under a vrf instance

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies BGP reachability inside a VRF instance. Configures BGP under a named VRF and confirms the remote network learnt via BGP is reachable within that VRF.

1366.2001.0.description:
Log TestSet setup outcome

Test-harness step (not a functional test): logs the per-test-set setup outcome before the set's functional cases run. Excluded from manual-test coverage mapping.

1366.2001.1.description:
VRF-Lite isolation

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies VRF-Lite traffic isolation. Confirms that traffic cannot leak between two named VRF instances, and that a named VRF is also isolated from the global/default VRF.

1366.2001.2.description:
VRF-Lite communication within the same instance

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies intra-VRF connectivity and inter-VRF isolation without routes. Confirms hosts within the same VRF instance can communicate directly, while hosts in different VRFs cannot reach each other in the absence of routes between them.

1366.2001.3.description:
VRF-Lite communication between VRFs with static routes

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies that adding inter-VRF static routes (route leaking) restores connectivity. Configures static routes between two named VRFs and between a named VRF and the global VRF, then confirms connectivity succeeds across those leaked routes.

1366.2001.4.description:
VRF-Lite isolation after VCS failovers

[Inferred behavior — case reported UNSUPPORTED on the current test setup; no recent PASS] Intended to verify that VRF-Lite isolation is preserved across VCS (Virtual Chassis Stacking) master failovers. Reported UNSUPPORTED because it requires a multi-member stack and the current setup is a single-member stack.

1366.2001.5.description:
VRF-Lite communication between VRFs with static routes after VCS failovers

[Inferred behavior — case reported UNSUPPORTED on the current test setup; no recent PASS] Intended to verify that inter-VRF connectivity via static routes is preserved across VCS master failovers. Reported UNSUPPORTED because it requires a multi-member stack and the current setup is a single-member stack.

1366.2001.6.description:
VRF-Lite with tagged VLANs

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies VRF-Lite behaviour over tagged VLANs. Ingressing traffic on a tagged VLAN, confirms inter-VRF connectivity works where static routes exist and that isolation between a named VRF and the global VRF still holds.

1366.2001.7.description:
VRF-Lite with management tools

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies that common management tools operate correctly within a VRF instance. Confirms ping, traceroute, SSH, and tcpdump all function for traffic scoped to a named VRF.

1366.2001.8.description:
VRF-Lite instance stress test

[Log-derived analysis] Stress-tests VRF instance creation and teardown. Repeatedly configures the maximum supported number of VRF instances, confirms each instance and its associated loopback interface are created, then deconfigures them all and confirms clean removal, cycling through multiple iterations.

1366.2001.9.description:
VRF-Lite max-static-routes

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies the per-VRF max-static-routes limit. Sets a static-route limit on one VRF instance, confirms the CLI warns and caps once the limit is exceeded, confirms a second instance is unaffected, then removes the limit and confirms it no longer applies.

1366.2001.10.description:
VRF-Lite max-fib-routes

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies the per-VRF max-fib-routes limit. Sets a FIB-route limit on one VRF instance, confirms dynamic routes are correctly capped and the breach is logged, confirms a second instance is unaffected, then removes the limit and confirms it no longer applies.

1366.2001.11.description:
VRF-Lite with ARP

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies ARP behaviour within VRF-Lite. Confirms a static ARP entry suppresses ARP requests during a ping, then confirms a dynamic ARP entry is learnt within a VRF instance and can be cleared.
